title.narrative: Bridges to Hope and Healing (BHH): Provision of MHPSS Services for Returnees, IDPs, and Vulnerable Communities in Kabul and Paktia, to improve well-being and social integration.

description.narrative: ltpgtHagar International’s Project Bridges to Hope and Healing (BHH), aims to support 36,398 direct beneficiaries from the returnee and host communities in the two targeted provinces (Kabul and Paktia). The project will address critical gaps in the delivery of high-quality Mental health and psychosocial services (MHPSS), by providing basic MHPSS services through two BHCs and three CHCs in Farza, Gulkhana, Bagrami, Shewaki and Deh Sabz, and two new, community-based centers in PD 6 Kabul and Deh Sabz district. Inclusive mental health and psychosocial health services will be supplemented by life skills sessions for women and youth, and strong referral pathways will be built across the different centers. We will also support with psychiatrists and counsellors, one District Hospital and one General hospital n Kabul and we will set up a specialist Mental Health Unit in Paktia. New MHPSS services in these hospitals will include the provision of essential psychotropic medication, counselling and in some places play therapy. In Paktia we will be setting up in patient services. lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project prioritizes assistance to returnees, IDPs, youth, women and People with Psychosocial disorders (PPSDs) and those with physical disabilities or others experiencing vulnerabilities. In Kabul BHH will connect with Hagar International’s existing women’s empowerment and community-based child protection programs, with potential for skills development and apprenticeships. lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtHagar’s community feedback and accountability mechanisms, and AWAAZ hotline number 410 will be leveraged to allow returnees to raise concerns or complaints, ensuring timely responses and fostering trust between communities and service providers. Gender-sensitive approaches will support female attendance at health services and community initiatives will reduce travel distance for female beneficiaries and encourage attendance for the most vulnerable, through the provision of dignity kits.lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtThe BHH project will be implemented in close coordination with the Health Cluster led by the World Health Organization (WHO), the Ministry of Public Health (MoPH), Provincial Public Health Directorates (PPHDs), local NGOs providing complementary services and existing health facilities. BHH will also work closely with communities, equipping Shura members to identify and refer PPSDs to our services, so that the project does not only meet the needs of PPSDs who present themselves to health facilities, but also to those in the community who have previously been unidentified or for whom stigma and taboos have prevented from help-seeking behaviors. lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtWith MHPSS as the core of our revised programming, Hagar will deploy 19 Counsellors 17 across the centers in Kabul province and two in Paktia. We will also deploy five psychiatrists. These medical professionals will be supported by Community Volunteers (CVs), who will be trained in PPSD identification, PSEA, disability awareness and referrals. CVs will work across each center in order to promote acceptance and reduce stigma around mental health and to build strong referral pathways.lt/pgt ltpgt ltbrgtlt/pgt
